newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco climbs as strike boosts nickel prices.
newsitem.headline: Inco climbs as strike boosts nickel prices.

text.p: Shares in Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd rose on Tuesday as nickel prices rallied after the company's workers in Sudbury, Ontario went on strike.
Inco stock was up 0.30 at 44.70 in late morning turnover of 100,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
About unionized 4,670 workers at the Sudbury operations went on strike at midnight after they voted 60.4 percent against a tentative contract agreement.

"Inco obviously is losing some production here. If it results in higher nickel prices, Inco's shares will be more sensitive to the nickel price than their immediate production numbers," one mining analyst said.
Asian buying pushed three-month nickel prices to a peak of US$7,330 per tonne after news of the Sudbury strike. Prices later settled down to close around US$7,180 on the London Exchange.
New York-based brokerage Prudential Securities on Tuesday upgraded its rating on Inco to buy from hold.
While news of the strike prompted volatile trading on metal markets, the Sudbury union said no date had been set for talks to resume.

"I think we've put the word out that we're prepared to sit down and meet at any time. We can't do any more than that," Gary Patterson, vice-president of local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Inco and union negotiators reached a tentative agreement on Friday, a day before workers had been scheduled to strike at midnight on Saturday.
But in Monday's ratification vote, the three-year contract offer was rejected by 2,638 of the 4,397 Sudbury workers who voted.
About 100 workers at Inco Ltd's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery voted 70 percent in favor of the contract offer.

According to Inco's production plan for the current fiscal year, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper, and about four million pounds of cobalt.
Inco officials were unavailable for comment.
